title: From younger to older grades
statement: Whether a teaching approach built for younger readers holds for older ones is untested, and one trial in an older grade is a probe, not proof.
detail: A service meeting record describes the reading project's material as early-reading pedagogy, plausible for primary and early middle school but not known to cover advanced comprehension; a sixth-grade course was assigned partly to learn how far the approach reaches, a suggestion that higher grades need less scaffolding was declined because it had never been tried, and high-school reading was called a complete unknown (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0130-incept-service-coe-catchup-2026-07-15.qmd`). The record's rule is never to describe the pedagogy or the trained model as grade-agnostic. To settle it: the same lesson design taught at an older grade and measured on a later test of new items.

evidence.quote: Do not describe this pedagogy or the trained model as grade-agnostic. Grade 6 is a probe, not proof.
